t:
(a) In General.—The Administrator of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration shall determine whether the March 2011, Tohoku earthquake and subsequent tsunami and the October 2012, hurricane Sandy each caused a severe marine debris event (as that term is defined in section 7(6) of the Marine Debris Act (33 U.S.C. 1956(6)), as amended by this Act). 
    (b) Deadline.—Not later than 30 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator shall provide the determination required under subsection (a) to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Natural Resources of the House of Representatives.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the Administrator's determination and its delivery to committees amount to a consultative process. But the determination is made by a federal official alone, and its only recipients are congressional committees, which are inside the federal government. No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public is consulted, heard, or given a right to challenge the decision.
fable.s: the Administrator shall provide the determination required under subsection (a) to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Natural Resources of the House of Representatives.

opus.w: The NOAA Administrator makes the severe marine debris determination alone and then reports it to congressional committees. Congress is inside the federal government, so this report is not participation. It might seem procedural enough to count, but the section never brings in anyone outside the federal government, whether by consultation, comment, hearing or a right to object.
opus.s: the Administrator shall provide the determination required under subsection (a) to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Natural Resources of the House of Representatives.
opus.b: **Tempting reading:** The section has the NOAA Administrator make a formal determination and then deliver it to congressional committees, which looks like a procedure with more than one party. But Congress and its committees are inside the federal government, and no state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is consulted before the determination is made.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Administrator to submit a determination to congressional committees. Congress is part of the federal government, so reporting to it is an intra-governmental action, not participation by outside parties. There is no requirement for public comment, hearings, or consultation with non-federal entities.
qwen_chat.s: Not later than 30 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator shall provide the determination required under subsection (a) to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Natural Resources of the House of Representatives.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Administrator must make a determination, there is an implicit process involving outside input. However, the text explicitly limits the output of this determination to congressional committees. Congress is inside the federal government. There is no mention of public comment, hearings, advisory boards with non-federal members, or consultation with states/tribes. Therefore, this is an internal government reporting requirement, not participation.
